findings.evidence: Lines 58–61 use only `hT.finiteDimensional_ker`; lines 66–69 use only `hT.finiteDimensional_coker` and `hT.isClosed_range`; lines 175–182 additionally use closedness of the range, never finite-dimensional cokernel.
findings.fix: Prove general splitting constructors for an arbitrary continuous linear map from the precise finite-dimensionality/closedness hypotheses, then derive the `IsFredholm` methods as wrappers.
findings.issue: All kernel-side declarations require `hT : IsFredholm T` but use only `finiteDimensional_ker` (plus closed range for the final equivalence); all range-side declarations use only `isClosed_range` and `finiteDimensional_coker`, unnecessarily requiring finite-dimensional kernel.

summary: The splitting API is unnecessarily restricted to Fredholm operators even though its two halves use strictly weaker, independent hypotheses.
